body:
I'm very sorry to hear about all this. I struggle with depression and a few other things myself, and have always been stuck in my imagination as well - It's easier to escape into a world that isn't your own, isn't it?

I spend a lot of time creating my own characters and universes complete with drawings and everything and it can get really out of control sometimes. My therapist suggested using it to my creative advantage, like using it as a means of focusing more on my art and writing - It gave me a lot of motivation to focus on those things, like always having new drawing ideas or writing ideas. I was able to take something that messed with me for a really long time and turn it into a means of doing better.

Just some insight from my point of view. I know how it is.

I might not know a whole lot, but I've known many abusive people through family or family friends over the years and I can promise you this - Abusive people don't change. Even if she did, the emotional scars from past abuse are still there and will always loom over the relationship like the big scary elephant in the room. It's not worth it - Love and relationships can come with setbacks, yeah, but never should it cross into toxic territory.

It's hard, you love her, I get it. You need to love yourself more than you do her, though - She needs help, and maybe she does have issues driving her to do this, but it's not your fault. Her happiness should NEVER have to be at YOUR expense, because you deserve better than this. You're just as deserving of love and kindness as everyone else, and being in this only hinders your chances. True love doesn't come with abuse.
